title: Early Adopter Health Index & Tactical Staffflow Playlet
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, tactical playlet to monitor early-adopter health and guide short-window staffing and decisioning for a staged product rollout. It blends a small KPI dashboard, a 72-hour staffing play, and quick rollback/mitigation heuristics intended for product-ops and SRE pairing during the first two weeks post-beta.

How to use this doc:
- Keep this doc pinned in the launch command channel.
- Update the KPI snapshot daily (am PST) until adopter cohort stabilizes for 14 days.
- Use the scoring guidance below to decide between throttle, canary hold, or rollback.

Scoring rubric (quick):
- Health Index = 0.35*RetentionScore + 0.25*ReliabilityScore + 0.20*LatencyScore + 0.10*CostScore + 0.10*CSATScore.
- Each component normalized 0..100. Target overall >= 80 to continue ramp. 60-80 requires mitigations and reduced ramp rate. <60 -> consider rollback.

Current observations (notes from last 24h):
- Latency p95 spiked to ~420ms for a small subset of long-sequence prompts between 03:00-06:00 UTC; traced to a misrouted batch queue on region-eu-2; auto-fallback to smaller model activated but increased costs.
- Two early adopters reported hallucination regressions in a narrow prompt family (see RDW-3121). Team assigned: Jin-Woo to own evaluation set and rollback candidate.
- Cache hit ratio below expected; runtime config shows prefix-caching disabled for the canary pool due to safety toggle.

Immediate tactical checklist (first 3 hours):
- [ ] Triage alert owner (on-call SRE) acknowledges in #prodops-launch (within 10m).
- [ ] Product-ops lead posts top-3 customer-impact notes (within 30m).
- [ ] If p95 latency > SLO *and* error rate > threshold: flip routing to fallthrough model variant (pre-approved fallback) and notify customers.
- [ ] Kick-off targeted regression eval run: sample set + 100 synthetic prompts across sequences. Owner: Jin-Woo (2h run).
- [ ] Update the KPI snapshot and mark deviation tags (latency, reliability, quality).

72-hour staffing rota (playlet):
- Shift pattern: product-ops lead (Priya) daily 09:00-13:00 PST; on-call SRE 24/7 handoffs via SRE rota; solutions eng Samir 11:00-19:00 PST for customer comms first week.
- Escalation chain: on-call SRE -> SRE principal -> platform eng lead -> CTO on pager if incident P0 > 30m unresolved.
- Daily stand (15m) at 08:30 PST (include SRE, product-ops, solutions-eng).

Rollback & containment criteria (fast heuristics):
- Automatic partial rollback (canary -> previous model) if: sustained p95 latency > 2x SLO for 30m AND adopter CSAT trend falling > 0.2 points/day from baseline.
- Manual full rollback if: errors escalate to > 50/10k requests OR severe data-safety regression confirmed by product + legal.
- When rolling back, always: 1) open a JIRA incident (use RDW-INC template), 2) capture full trace exports, 3) annotate the deploy with rollback tag and rationale.

Mitigations to try before rollback:
- Re-enable prefix caching for the canary pool (if safe) to improve cost and latency for repetitive prompts. Owner: Marco (1h).
- Move heavy long-sequence traffic to a dedicated pool with aggressive batching (temp smoothing window 3s). Owner: Platform Eng (release ticket RDW-3200).
- Throttle new adopter sign-up funnel for 4 hours while stability fixes are validated. Owner: Priya (product ops).

Simulation plan (quick smoke):
- Nightly smoke job (run 02:00 UTC) that replays the top 1% longest sequences at 2x traffic for 30m to validate throughput and kernel selection. If failure rate > 3% -> tag for SRE triage.
- Shadow run: route 10% of canary requests to a parallel pool with cache enabled for 24h; compare cost/latency/quality deltas.

Customer comms snippets (templates):
- "We detected an instability affecting a small set of requests between X and Y; we have applied a mitigation and are closely monitoring. Expected fix ETA: 4h. If you notice degraded responses please reply to this thread'"
- For severe regressions: "We are rolling back a recent change to restore reliability. No customer data is affected. We'll follow up with post-mortem and mitigation plan."

Post-mortem anchors (what we capture):
- Timeline of events, contributing factors (infra config, model change, traffic pattern), exact impact numerics (requests, affected adopters), mitigation decisions taken, long-term action items with owners.

Action items (short list):
- Priya: throttle new signups for next 4 hours if Health Index < 70 (today). Due: ASAP.
- Marco: try toggling prefix cache for canary pool and report delta. Due: 1h.
- Jin-Woo: assemble 120-case evaluation harness and run regression tests; post results to RDW-3121. Due: 6h.
- Samir: prep customer comms and own thread responses for top-5 pilot customers. Due: 2h.

Notes & open questions (working):
- Is our fallback model variant validated for hallucination regression? Quick QA required.
- Should we add a cost-safety throttle to platform routing to automatically reduce max tokens for low-tier adopters during spikes? (Discuss in retro).

Appendix: short glossary
- Health Index: composite score for pilot stability and value (not a full SRE SLA).
- Canaries: small, pinned pool of capacity used for early adopter traffic.
- Prefix caching: runtime cache for repeated prompt prefixes to reduce cost/latency.

End of playlet. Update this doc after each incident iteration and push latest snapshot to Confluence reference page.
notes: Design intent: very tactical, low-friction doc for the first two weeks of an early adopter cohort.
Keep change history in Confluence and mark finalized mitigations for runbook inclusion.
This doc should live alongside the main launch tracker but remain intentionally lightweight to avoid duplication.
